Employees who arrive on time, without working out the way

From the airport to the apartment, from the apartment to the work site, and for every team journey in between: we organise your employees' travel in the Paris region and coordinate it with their housing.

Why transport is part of housing

An employee landing at Charles de Gaulle at 10 pm with two suitcases, not knowing where the apartment is or how to get there, starts the assignment tired and annoyed. A worker who needs two buses and a suburban train to reach a poorly served site arrives late, or not at all. Transport is not a logistical detail: it is what makes housing usable.

So we never separate the two. We choose the housing around your employee's journeys first, then organise the journeys that remain. Everything sits on the same quote and is followed by the same person.

What we organise

Airport and station transfers

A driver waits for your employee at Charles de Gaulle, Orly or Beauvais, or at the station (Gare du Nord, Gare de Lyon, Montparnasse, Gare de l'Est), name on a sign, and takes them to their door. No taxi queue, no app to install, no surprise on the price.

Daily commutes

Navigo travel pass or tickets handed over on arrival, recurring chauffeured rides for unsocial hours, a shuttle for crews going to the same site. We fit the solution to the assignment's real hours.

Team travel

Site visits, workshops, client meetings, induction days: a vehicle and driver for the whole team, booked on request and invoiced on the assignment's quote.

How we coordinate housing and journeys

Before proposing a property we calculate the real commute to the workplace, at the hours your employee actually travels: a flat fifteen minutes from the site beats a nicer flat an hour away.

Then we look at what is missing. An industrial site with poor public transport? A shuttle or a vehicle. Night shifts? Chauffeured rides. A team split across two sites? A common pick-up point. Every solution is written into the quote with its cost, so you can decide.

The first journey is the one that counts

The arrival transfer is when your employee forms an opinion of the assignment. A driver waiting, a calm ride, arriving at a door where the keys are ready: the assignment starts well.

We plan the reverse too: the return to the airport or station at the end, with the check-out inventory arranged the same day if needed. For employees who fly home at weekends, we can set up recurring transfers on fixed days and times.

Airports and stations: what to know

Charles de Gaulle is about forty kilometres north-east of Paris: allow forty-five minutes to well over an hour by car depending on traffic, or about thirty-five minutes on the RER B suburban train to the centre. Orly, to the south, is closer, but the journey depends a lot on the final destination and the time of day. Beauvais, used by some low-cost airlines, is more than an hour away. Paris taxis apply regulated flat fares from the airports, which avoids nasty surprises, but the queue can be long at peak times and nobody is waiting for your employee at the exit.

For arrivals by train, Gare du Nord, Gare de l'Est, Gare de Lyon and Montparnasse are all in central Paris and well connected to the metro. A chauffeured transfer remains worthwhile for people with luggage, late arrivals and housing outside Paris. We choose the most sensible option for each arrival with you, and write it into the quote.

What we take into account

Paris itself is easy by public transport, provided you live in the right place. The rest of the region often needs a vehicle.

Real working hours
A site that starts at 7 am, a consultant finishing at 9 pm, a crew on three shifts: the solutions are not the same.
Access to the site
Business parks, logistics platforms, sites on the outskirts: we check how you actually get there, and when the last train runs.
Number of people
A driver for one person, a shuttle for twelve: the cost per person changes a lot, and we work it out for you.
The unexpected
Strikes, roadworks, delayed flights: we track your employee's arrival and adjust the transfer if the plane is late.
Budget
Travel pass, ride-hailing, private driver, shuttle: we propose several levels and you choose.

How it works

  1. 1

    You send us flights and schedules

    Flight or train number, arrival time, number of people and bags, address of the work site.

  2. 2

    We organise the journeys

    Arrival transfer, daily solution, team travel if needed: everything appears on the quote, with the housing.

  3. 3

    Your employees receive the details

    Driver's name, meeting point, travel passes, directions to the site: by email and message before departure.

  4. 4

    We stay reachable

    For the whole stay, for a schedule change, an extra ride or an early return.

Transport questions

Can you organise transfers only, without housing?

Yes, if your employees are already housed. But there is real value in giving us both: we choose the housing around the commute.

What if the flight is delayed?

We track arrivals. The driver is informed and waits for your employee, at no extra charge within the limit stated in the quote.

Do you provide rental vehicles?

For crews that need to be autonomous on a site, we can arrange a van or a rental car delivered to the accommodation. Mention it when we prepare the quote.

Are daily journeys invoiced to the company?

Yes, like everything else: it all goes through your company's quote and invoice. Your employees pay nothing up front and you have no expense claims to process.
